rounds.proof_sketch: Input spec fixes dtype=float32 → scalar_t=float → val3 is float → (float)val3 is a no-op cast → fabsf((float)val3) ≡ fabsf(val3) for all float values
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation removes an explicit (float) cast that is applied to a variable val3 of type scalar_t. Since the input specification fixes the dtype at torch.float32, the AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES macro always instantiates the kernel with scalar_t=float. When scalar_t is float, casting a float to float is a semantic no-op that produces identical bit patterns. The fabsf() function receives the same float value in both original and mutated code paths. No possible float32 input value can trigger any difference because the cast operation itself is redundant.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation only matters when scalar_t=double (torch.float64), which would require changing the input dtype specification. With the fixed float32 dtype, the explicit cast is always a no-op.
rounds.recommendations: When testing cast-removal mutations, ensure dtype variations (float32, float64) are included in the test matrix if the kernel uses AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES and the contract permits dtype flexibility. For fixed-dtype contracts, such mutations may be semantically equivalent and should be classified as equivalent mutants rather than surviving mutants.
